balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Commerzbank AG: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Commerzbank AG: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Commerzbank AG: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Commerzbank AG: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Commerzbank AG: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Commerzbank AG: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Commerzbank AG: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Commerzbank AG: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

incomeMix.title: Net interest income vs net fee & commission income
incomeMix.content:
Net interest income (NII) is interest earned on loans and securities less interest paid on deposits and debt; net fee & commission income is advisory, payments and account fees -- income with no direct rate exposure.

For Commerzbank AG: NII is about 60% of total income and rode the 2022-24 ECB hiking cycle up (€4.8bn FY2021 to €8.3bn FY2024); it is now flat to slightly down (9M-2025 -1.2% YoY) as rates fall. Fee income is the steadier, rate-insensitive line Momentum is trying to grow.

What to watch:

  • NII rolling over faster than the structural hedge offsets
  • Fee income's share of the mix rising (reduces rate sensitivity)

efficiency.title: Cost-to-income ratio and credit impairment charge
efficiency.content:
The cost-to-income ratio is operating expenses divided by total income -- the core bank efficiency metric. The credit impairment charge (risk result) is the expected-credit-loss provision taken against the loan book in the period.

For Commerzbank AG: Momentum targets cost-to-income toward 52% by FY2028 through headcount cuts (3,900 roles). The risk result has been low and stable recently but can double in a downturn -- it hit €1.75bn in FY2020.

What to watch:

  • Cost-to-income drifting away from the Momentum glide path
  • A sudden jump in the impairment charge signalling a German SME/export credit downturn or mBank CHF-mortgage litigation costs

returns.title: Return on equity and book value per share
returns.content:
ROE (reported, pre-AT1/NCI adjustment) is net income over average shareholders' equity. Book value per share is shareholders' equity divided by shares outstanding -- the per-share anchor the DCF's P/B sanity check is measured against.

For Commerzbank AG: ROE around 9-10% is still below the 10.75% cost of equity used in the valuation; Momentum targets about 15% net RoTE by FY2028. Book value per share has compounded only about 2.7%/yr over 5 years because buybacks shrink total equity even as per-share book rises.

What to watch:

  • ROE crossing the cost of equity on a sustained basis, not one quarter
  • Book value per share growth versus the buyback pace (shrinking share count flatters the per-share figure even if total equity is flat)

capitalRatios.title: CET1, Tier 1 and total capital ratios
capitalRatios.content:
CET1 (Common Equity Tier 1) is the strictest capital ratio -- core equity over risk-weighted assets. Tier 1 adds AT1 instruments; total capital adds Tier 2 subordinated debt. All three are regulatory solvency measures, not valuation inputs.

For Commerzbank AG: the DCF targets a 13.5% CET1 ratio and treats capital above that as distributable to shareholders (buybacks/dividends); capital needed to fund RWA growth is retained rather than paid out. The AT1 coupons that Tier 1 (but not CET1) reflects are deducted before arriving at the FCFE the model discounts.

What to watch:

  • CET1 ratio relative to the 13.5% target and the SREP/MDA minimum
  • Risk-weighted assets growing faster than capital (dilutes the ratio even with flat capital)

dcf.base_sublabel: Owner FCF — after SBC, interest income & leases
dcf.model_approach_note: The multiples sanity check tripped: the original probability-weighted value of €36.25 implied 1.41x book, against a 10-year maximum of 0.72x (FY2024). One fix pass was applied. The cost of equity got an explicit +0.75pt premium for the pending UniCredit control decision and residual credit-cycle risk (base 10.75%, bear 11.75%, bull 10.25%). Earnings growth after the FY2028 Momentum plan, and terminal growth, were capped at the 2.4% through-cycle income CAGR. The weighted value fell to €31.87 (bear €22.12 / base €32.42 / bull €40.53), implying 1.24x book and 3.4x sales. That still exceeds the 1.08x trip line, and it is kept there on purpose. The historical band (0.23–0.72x) was set while Commerzbank earned 0–8% on tangible equity, below its cost of capital, and ends before the 2025 re-rating driven by UniCredit's approach and the Momentum upgrade. Forcing a pass would mean assuming returns near the bear case. The investment framing is income plus modest growth, not a re-rating story. At €36.27 the stock trades about 14% above the weighted value and about 70% above the €21.53 entry price at a 15% hurdle. The price already assumes about 14.5% sustained returns on tangible equity, close to the full 15% Momentum target. Upside from here depends mostly on UniCredit paying a control premium, not on standalone value.
